question.problem: Determine the equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z={y}^{2}-{x}^{2}y$ at the point $(1,0,0).$
question.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=f(x,y)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ on the surface can be written as

$$
z-{z}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0}).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2}-{x}^{2}y) \\  & =-2xy \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}-{x}^{2}y) \\  & =2y-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y)=(1,0):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,0) & =-2(1)(0)=0 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,0) & =2(0)-{1}^{2}=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-0 & =(x-1)\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,0)+(y-0)\frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,0) \\ z & =0(x-1)-y \\ z & =-y \\ y+z & =0\end{aligned}
$$
